newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late rubber stable, watches Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late rubber stable, watches Thailand.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were mostly stable in late trading on Thursday, with players critical of developments in Thailand.
Thai Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol, who chairs the natural rubber policy committee, said the government rubber intervention scheme would be extended by three months to October.

He said the government would not accept delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber bought from traders to cut losses, but was expected to spend three billion baht in the next three months to prop up rubber prices in the domestic market.

"It seems to be a political move," one industry source said. "Also, by announcing how much it is going to spend and for how long, Thailand has taken out the speculative elements which drive the market. It has given the game away."
"The move will help the markets a little, but I think a remedy will only come after the summer months," he added. "The Thai move indicates a lack of knowledge about the market."
Traders said they were monitoring developments in Thailand and also in Malaysia, where prices were already at a discount to Indonesian values.
"Malaysian SMR20 is at a discount to Indonesia's SIR20 and obviously buyers will be heading to Malaysia," one said. "Local prices will have to adjust lower to be competitive."
"I will be watching closely how the Thai market moves following the government's decision," he added. "There seems to be a certain amount of politics involved."
Traders said the Indonesian market was quiet on the back of thin buying interest.
They said September shipment SIR20 was quoted at 43.00-43.25 cents/lb fob Medan, 43.00 cents fob Palembang and 42.50-75 cents fob Jambi.
